The friendship had been built on a dozen films as co-stars from 1975 onward, Deewaar, Kabhie Kabhie, Kaala Patthar, Suhaag and Namak Halaal among them, none of which the roster can count because acting is not a tracked function. His is the most Bachchan-dense article in the roster and the widest gap between a recorded collaboration and a real one. Graded High.

name: Sooraj R. Barjatya
career_background: Born in Bombay on 22 February 1964, a filmmaker whose films are rooted in familial ties, traditional values and Indian domestic ritual. He is chairman of Rajshri Productions, the company his grandfather Tarachand Barjatya formed in 1947, and began his career as an assistant director to Mahesh Bhatt.
debut: Maine Pyar Kiya (1989), a top-grossing romantic drama.
major_works: Maine Pyar Kiya (1989); Hum Aapke Hain Koun..! (1994); Hum Saath-Saath Hain (1999); Vivah (2006); Prem Ratan Dhan Payo (2015); Uunchai (2022)
recurring_themes: The extended family as the unit of drama — weddings, obligation, reconciliation — with conflict resolved rather than punished, and no villain in the usual sense.
creative_style: The purest expression of the Rajshri house style: long, ceremonious, song-filled family films made for audiences who watch them together, deliberately free of violence and sex.
major_awards: The National Film Award for Best Direction for Uunchai (2022).
historical_importance: Hum Aapke Hain Koun..! became the highest-grossing Indian film to that point and reset the commercial template for the family musical in the 1990s.
relationship_with_actor: One film, made 49 years after his grandfather's. Uunchai (2022), for which he won the National Film Award for Best Direction, is an ensemble drama about four elderly friends who trek to Everest Base Camp to scatter the ashes of the fourth; Bachchan leads an ensemble with Anupam Kher, Boman Irani and Parineeti Chopra. It is a late-career film explicitly about age, friendship and the body's limits, and it came after a seven-year hiatus in Barjatya's own career.
most_important_collaboration: Uunchai (2022), his only film with Bachchan.
biography: Sooraj R. Barjatya inherited Rajshri Productions from his grandfather and made it the home of the Hindi family film, with Maine Pyar Kiya, Hum Aapke Hain Koun..! — for a time the highest-grossing Indian film ever — Hum Saath-Saath Hain, Vivah and Prem Ratan Dhan Payo: long, ceremonious pictures with no villains and no violence. His single Bachchan film, Uunchai, won him the National Film Award for Best Direction and sends four old friends to Everest Base Camp with the ashes of a fifth. It completes a three-generation link inside this roster: his grandfather Tarachand Barjatya (PERSON-233) produced Piya Ka Ghar and Saudagar with Bachchan in 1972 and 1973, when Bachchan was unknown, and the grandson directed him in 2022 at 80, both under the same banner, Rajshri Productions (PERSON-096). No other family in this roster spans the filmography so completely. Graded High.

name: Sudhendu Roy
career_background: Born in Pabna in the Bengal Presidency in 1921 and died in Mumbai in 1999, he was principally an art director and production designer, celebrated for his realistic art direction in Bimal Roy's films — Sujata (1959), Madhumati (1959) and Bandini (1963) — and later for glossier work on Subhash Ghai's Karz (1980) and Karma (1986) and Yash Chopra's Silsila (1981), Chandni (1989) and Lamhe (1991). He directed only twice.
debut: As director, Uphaar (1971).
major_works: As art director: Sujata (1959); Madhumati (1959); Bandini (1963); Silsila (1981); Chandni (1989). As director: Uphaar (1971); Saudagar (1973)
recurring_themes: Both of his films as director are literary adaptations of Bengali material about rural poverty and the use of women's labour and bodies.
creative_style: A designer's eye applied to direction: spare, observational films drawn from short stories rather than from film convention, and made outside the commercial idiom of their moment.
major_awards: The Filmfare Award for Best Art Direction three times — Madhumati (1959), Mere Mehboob (1964) and Sagina (1975).
historical_importance: One of the most important art directors in Hindi cinema, spanning Bimal Roy's realism and Yash Chopra's glamour across four decades; both films he directed were India's official entry to the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
relationship_with_actor: One film, and it is one of the least flattering parts Bachchan ever took. Saudagar (1973), adapted from Narendranath Mitra's Bengali story Ras and produced by Tarachand Barjatya, casts him as Moti, a jaggery-maker who marries an older widow, played by Nutan, for her skill at boiling gur, then discards her for a younger woman once he can afford to and tries to return when his business fails. It was not a commercial success but was much praised and became India's Academy Award entry. Roy also art-directed Silsila, another Bachchan film in this filmography, in a capacity the roster does not track.
most_important_collaboration: Saudagar (1973), his only film as Bachchan's director and an Indian Academy Award submission.
biography: Sudhendu Roy spent his career as one of Hindi cinema's great art directors, from the realism he built for Bimal Roy in Sujata, Madhumati and Bandini to the gloss of Yash Chopra's Silsila, Chandni and Lamhe, winning three Filmfare Awards for art direction. He directed only two films, and both were sent by India to the Academy Awards: Uphaar (1971), from Tagore's Samapti, which gave Jaya Bhaduri her first solo lead and was commissioned by Tarachand Barjatya of Rajshri; and Saudagar (1973), from a Bengali story by Narendranath Mitra, in which Amitabh Bachchan plays a gur-maker who marries a widow for her labour and throws her over when a prettier prospect becomes affordable. It is a coldly unsympathetic role, taken before Zanjeer made such casting impossible. Roy also designed Silsila, a Bachchan film the roster cannot count, art direction not being a tracked function. Graded High.

name: Sultan Ahmed
career_background: Born in Lucknow in the United Provinces and died in Tehran, Iran, on 22 May 2002. A director and producer of the 1970s and 1980s known for films about dacoits, he served the Indian Motion Picture Producers' Association from 1990 to 1994. His sons are Ali Akbar and Ali Abbas Sultan Ahmed.
debut: Heera, for which he received his first award, from the Uttar Pradesh Film Journalist Association in 1973.
major_works: Heera; Ganga Ki Saugandh (1978); Dharam Kanta; Daata
recurring_themes: Dacoit films — the bandit in the ravines as a figure of wronged honour — which is the genre he is identified with almost exclusively.
creative_style: A director of large-canvas rural melodrama with major stars, working repeatedly in one genre.
major_awards: First award for Heera from the Uttar Pradesh Film Journalist Association (1973); a certificate of merit for Ganga Ki Saugandh from Tashkent (1979); the K. Asif Memorial Award for 'Big Thinking' from the Bombay Film Awards Association (1982–83); the Punjabi Kala Sangam award for Daata, presented by President Giani Zail Singh.
historical_importance: One of the principal makers of the dacoit film in its 1970s heyday, and an office-holder in the industry's producers' association.
relationship_with_actor: One film. Ganga Ki Saugandh (1978) is a dacoit drama in which Bachchan plays Jeeva, a villager driven to banditry by a tyrannical landlord; the article records that Ahmed 'went on to sign Amitabh Bachchan and Rekha' for it, and it earned him a certificate of merit at Tashkent in 1979. The workbook records no Romances row for the film, its sources being too thin to describe the relationship honestly.
most_important_collaboration: Ganga Ki Saugandh (1978), his only film with Bachchan.
biography: Sultan Ahmed made dacoit films — Heera, Ganga Ki Saugandh, Daata — and did so with the biggest stars available, directing Sunil Dutt, Rajesh Khanna, Jeetendra, Mithun Chakraborty and, in Ganga Ki Saugandh, Amitabh Bachchan and Rekha. He collected an unusual spread of honours, from a Tashkent certificate of merit to the K. Asif Memorial Award for 'Big Thinking', and served the producers' association in the early 1990s before dying in Tehran in 2002. Ganga Ki Saugandh is his only film here, made at the height of Bachchan's stardom and pairing him again with Rekha. One point of record: his Wikipedia article's short description, as fetched for this project, had been vandalised to read 'Indian Hindu Phobic film director'. It is disregarded entirely — the body of the article is unaffected and is what this row rests on — and it is noted only because the short description is the single field this project has relied on most heavily for verification. No birth date is given anywhere in the article. Graded Medium.

name: Suneel Darshan
career_background: An Indian filmmaker, director, producer and writer working in Hindi cinema. His brother is the director Dharmesh Darshan. His article gives no birth date and almost no career detail.
debut: Not established from the sources.
major_works: Ek Rishtaa: The Bond of Love (2001)
recurring_themes: Family melodrama built around duty between generations, so far as the single documented film indicates.
creative_style: No source characterises his direction.
major_awards: None located.
historical_importance: Not established by the available sources.
relationship_with_actor: One film, which he directed, produced and wrote the story for. Ek Rishtaa: The Bond of Love (2001) casts Bachchan as Vijay Kapoor, a factory owner whose sons disappoint him, with Akshay Kumar, Karisma Kapoor and Juhi Chawla — the film his article refers to when it notes the cast. It sits in the difficult stretch either side of 2000 when Bachchan was rebuilding a career after ABCL's collapse, and the workbook records it as a spouse-only relationship with no Romances row.
most_important_collaboration: Ek Rishtaa: The Bond of Love (2001), his only film with Bachchan.
biography: Suneel Darshan directs, produces and writes Hindi films, and his brother Dharmesh Darshan does the same, but his Wikipedia article is among the poorest in this roster: no birth date, no filmography in the fetched text, a lead that opens mid-sentence with a stray image caption from a family prayer meeting, and an unexplained assertion that he was 'born into Bhatt family' which nothing else in the article supports and which is not repeated as fact here. His one credit in this filmography is Ek Rishtaa: The Bond of Love (2001), which he directed, produced and devised, casting Bachchan as a patriarch and factory owner opposite Akshay Kumar, Karisma Kapoor and Juhi Chawla. The film belongs to the run of early-2000s work in which Bachchan played fathers to younger stars while rebuilding his position after the failure of his own company. Graded Low.

name: T. J. Gnanavel
career_background: Born in Chennai, a graduate of Loyola College, Chennai, with a PhD in Tamil literature. He worked as a journalist — at the magazine Ananda Vikatan — before entering cinema, beginning as a dialogue writer on Raththa Sarithiram (2010) and Payanam (2011) and then as an assistant director.
debut: Kootathil Oruthan (2017), a comedy with Ashok Selvan and Priya Anand, which drew average reviews.
major_works: Kootathil Oruthan (2017); Jai Bhim (2021); Vettaiyan (2024)
recurring_themes: Law, caste and custodial power — the courtroom and the police station as the places where the state shows what it really is.
creative_style: A journalist's cinema: films built on documented cases, argued in procedural detail and staged with restraint rather than spectacle, even when a major star is at the centre.
major_awards: None recorded in the fetched article.
historical_importance: Jai Bhim, based on a case handled by Justice K. Chandru, was among the most widely discussed Indian films of its year and brought a custodial-violence case to an international streaming audience.
relationship_with_actor: One film, and it is a late-career first. Vettaiyan (2024) is Amitabh Bachchan's Tamil-language debut, made at 81, in which he appears opposite Rajinikanth as a co-lead — the two biggest stars of the Hindi and Tamil industries sharing a film about encounter killings. Gnanavel wrote and directed it, carrying into a mass star vehicle the concerns of Jai Bhim, which he had built from a case he first encountered as a journalist interviewing Justice K. Chandru.
most_important_collaboration: Vettaiyan (2024), his only film with Bachchan and Bachchan's Tamil debut.
biography: T. J. Gnanavel holds a doctorate in Tamil literature and worked as a journalist at Ananda Vikatan before writing dialogue and then directing. His second film, Jai Bhim (2021), drawn from a case handled by Justice K. Chandru — whom he had interviewed years earlier as a reporter — made him one of the most talked-about directors in India for its account of custodial violence against a tribal community. He then made Vettaiyan (2024), which brought the same preoccupation with police impunity into a Rajinikanth vehicle and gave Amitabh Bachchan his Tamil-language debut at 81, a late first this workbook records alongside his Gujarati debut in 2022. A small coincidence connects him to PERSON-289: S. S. Balan, who directed Bachchan in Sanjog in 1972, spent decades as editor of Ananda Vikatan, the magazine Gnanavel later worked for. His Wikipedia article is a single sentence, so the substance here comes from a supplementary search. Graded Medium.

name: Umesh Shukla
industry: Hindi and Gujarati cinema and theatre
career_background: An Indian actor and director working in Hindi films and in Gujarati theatre, active since 1994. He acted before he directed, notably in a villain role in Mithun Chakraborty's Yaar Gaddar, and has acted in and directed many Gujarati plays, among them Kanjee Viruddha Kanjee.
debut: Dhoondte Reh Jaaoge, presented by UTV Motion Pictures and Bindass.
major_works: Dhoondte Reh Jaaoge; Oh My God (2012); 102 Not Out (2018)
recurring_themes: Adaptations of Gujarati stage material into Hindi films, usually comedies with an argument inside them — a man suing God, a father outliving his son's pessimism.
creative_style: A theatre director's approach to film: small casts, single premises, dialogue-driven scenes, and source material taken from the Gujarati stage.
major_awards: None located.
historical_importance: Oh My God, adapted from his own Gujarati play, is among the most commercially successful Indian films built on a satirical religious premise.
relationship_with_actor: One film. 102 Not Out (2018), adapted from Saumya Joshi's Gujarati play, casts Bachchan as Dattatraya Vakharia, a 102-year-old man determined to break a longevity record who sets about curing his gloomy 75-year-old son of premature old age; Rishi Kapoor plays the son, and it was the pair's first film together in 27 years. It is a two-hander that depends entirely on the performances, which is the register Shukla works in.
most_important_collaboration: 102 Not Out (2018), his only film with Bachchan.
biography: Umesh Shukla came to film from the Gujarati stage, where he acted and directed, and his best-known films are both adaptations of Gujarati plays: Oh My God, from his own Kanjee Viruddha Kanjee, and 102 Not Out, from Saumya Joshi's play. The second is his only credit in this filmography and it is a notable one — Bachchan as a 102-year-old chasing a longevity record and trying to jolt his 75-year-old son out of a premature old age, with Rishi Kapoor opposite him for the first time in 27 years. The film was the second release of Sony's relaunched Indian production arm, SPE Films India (PERSON-227), which boarded it specifically for the Bachchan–Kapoor pairing. His Wikipedia article is short, gives no birth date and contains a garbled passage, so the row leans on the film's own article. Graded Medium.

name: Vijay Anand
career_background: Born in Gurdaspur, Punjab, on 22 January 1934 and died in Mumbai on 23 February 2004. Known as Goldie Anand, he was a filmmaker, producer, screenwriter, editor and actor, and part of the Anand family; he made most of his films for the family banner, Navketan Films.
debut: Directing from the late 1950s; his major run began with Guide (1965).
major_works: Guide (1965); Teesri Manzil (1966); Jewel Thief (1967); Johny Mera Naam (1970); Ram Balram (1980)
recurring_themes: Suspense and disguise, and song sequences conceived as narrative rather than interruption — he is widely regarded as the finest picturiser of songs in Hindi cinema.
creative_style: A writer-director who also cut his own films, with a command of screen geography and rhythm; Raj Khosla's article names him with Guru Dutt as an Indian follower of the Hitchcock school of mystery-suspense.
major_awards: Filmfare Awards for Best Director and Best Dialogue for Guide (1965), and for Best Screenplay and Best Editing for Johny Mera Naam (1970); BFJA awards as Best Editor for Johny Mera Naam (1970) and Double Cross (1972).
historical_importance: One of the most technically accomplished directors of Hindi cinema's classical period, and the maker of Guide, among the most admired Indian films of the 1960s.
relationship_with_actor: One film, and it comes long after his best work. Ram Balram (1980) casts Bachchan as Inspector Balram Singh opposite Dharmendra, in a co-lead; Anand directed, wrote and edited it, and Tito Juneja produced it under Navjeevan Films. The workbook records no Romances row for the film, the sources being too thin. His article does not mention Amitabh Bachchan — its one Bachchan reference is to Jaya Bachchan, opposite whom he acted in Kora Kagaz (1974).
most_important_collaboration: Ram Balram (1980), his only film with Bachchan.
biography: Vijay 'Goldie' Anand directed Guide, Teesri Manzil, Jewel Thief and Johny Mera Naam, won Filmfare Awards for directing, dialogue, screenplay and editing, and is remembered above all for staging songs as narrative rather than as decoration. Most of his work was made for Navketan, the family banner he shared with his brothers Dev and Chetan Anand. His single film with Amitabh Bachchan, Ram Balram (1980), belongs to a much later and lesser phase: an action melodrama pairing Bachchan with Dharmendra, which Anand directed, wrote and edited himself, produced by Tito Juneja (PERSON-234) under Navjeevan Films. His own article does not mention Amitabh at all, referring only to Jaya Bachchan, his co-star in Kora Kagaz. The infobox repeats his birth date in the death field, so the dates come from the lead. Graded High.

name: Vijay Krishna Acharya
career_background: Born in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, a director, screenwriter and dialogue writer working in Hindi films and television since 2004. He is married to Anusheh Khan. His article gives no birth year and lists no films in the fetched text.
debut: Not established from the article.
major_works: Thugs of Hindostan (2018) is the only title confirmed from the sources used here.
recurring_themes: Not characterised by the available sources.
creative_style: No source in this project's material describes his direction.
major_awards: None recorded in the article.
historical_importance: Not established by the fetched article, which is unusually thin for a director of films at this budget level.
relationship_with_actor: One film, and it is among the most expensive failures in Hindi cinema. Thugs of Hindostan (2018) casts Bachchan as Khudabaksh Azaad, a rebel leader fighting the East India Company, opposite Aamir Khan — the first film to pair the two since a brief shared credit decades earlier — with Katrina Kaif and Fatima Sana Shaikh. Acharya wrote and directed it. The workbook records no Romances row for Bachchan in the film, and its reported budget figures are disputed, with Wikipedia's range kept in the film's notes.
most_important_collaboration: Thugs of Hindostan (2018), his only film with Bachchan.
biography: Vijay Krishna Acharya writes and directs Hindi films and has worked in the industry since 2004, but his Wikipedia article as cached for this project is remarkably uninformative: a one-sentence lead, no birth year, no filmography in the extract, no awards and no mention of Bachchan. What can be established is his single credit here, Thugs of Hindostan, which he wrote and directed — a period adventure starring Amitabh Bachchan as a rebel commander against the East India Company alongside Aamir Khan, made at one of the largest budgets in the industry's history and remembered chiefly for the scale of its commercial failure. The film's reported budget is disputed between trade and Wikipedia figures, a conflict the workbook records in the film's own notes rather than resolving. Graded Low, the person being effectively undocumented even though the film is not.

name: Vikram Bhatt
career_background: A director, producer, screenwriter and actor active since 1982, and a member of the Bhatt film family: his father is the cinematographer Pravin Bhatt, his grandfather was Vijay Bhatt, his uncle is Arun Bhatt and his first cousin the composer Chirantan Bhatt. He was creative head of ASA Productions and Enterprises until he resigned in 2014, and co-founded Loneranger Productions, under which many of his films were made.
debut: Directing from the early 1990s; his breakthrough was Ghulam (1998).
major_works: Ghulam (1998); Raaz (2002) and the Raaz series; Aetbaar (2004)
recurring_themes: Horror and erotic thriller, frequently adapted from Hollywood originals, with a recurring interest in possession and obsession.
creative_style: A high-volume genre director who works quickly and cheaply in horror, and who has produced a large body of work for the Bhatt family's production houses.
major_awards: Filmfare Award nominations for Best Director for Ghulam (1999) and Raaz (2003); both entries in his awards table are nominations, so no win is asserted.
historical_importance: The Raaz films are the most durable Hindi horror franchise, and Bhatt is among the most prolific directors of his generation.
relationship_with_actor: One film. Aetbaar (2004) casts Bachchan as Dr Ranveer Malhotra, a father whose daughter's boyfriend turns out to be dangerously obsessive — an unofficial reworking of Fear, with John Abraham as the stalker. Bachchan plays the protective father rather than the centre of the story, and the film is one of the small 2004 releases that Box Office India did not list.
most_important_collaboration: Aetbaar (2004), his only film with Bachchan.
biography: Vikram Bhatt belongs to one of Hindi cinema's oldest film families — grandson of Vijay Bhatt, son of the cinematographer Pravin Bhatt — and has directed since the early 1990s at a pace few match, with Ghulam and the Raaz horror series his best-known work and two Filmfare Best Director nominations to his name, both unconverted. His single Bachchan film is Aetbaar (2004), a thriller reworking the premise of Fear in which Bachchan plays a doctor whose daughter is pursued by an obsessive young man, played by John Abraham. It is a supporting-shaped lead in a genre film, and it belongs to the period when Bachchan was working at extremely high volume across every register available to him. His cousin Chirantan Bhatt is among the credited composers of Boss (FILM-217) in this filmography, but with one credit he did not meet the roster threshold. Graded High.

name: Vishal Desai
career_background: An actor associated with Baghban, Baabul and the television show Banda Yeh Bindaas Hai who worked as an assistant director to Ravi Chopra and was reported in 2007 to be moving into direction. No birth date or further career detail could be located.
debut: Not established as a director.
major_works: None confirmed as director; he assisted on Baghban (2003).
recurring_themes: Not determinable.

major_awards: None located.
historical_importance: None established.
relationship_with_actor: One credit, and it is disputed. Baghban's Wikipedia infobox lists four names in its director field — Ravi Chopra, Harish Razdan, Vishal Desai and Yatin Dang — and phase 1 copied all four into the Films sheet, which is why he has a row. Every other source, including that article's own prose, Variety, Letterboxd, TMDB and Indiancine.ma, credits Ravi Chopra alone, and a 2007 trade piece describes Desai as having assisted Chopra on the film. Bachchan plays Raj Malhotra, the retired bank clerk turned away by his sons, in one of the largest hits of his late career; there is no evidence Desai directed him.
most_important_collaboration: Baghban (2003), his only credit.
biography: Vishal Desai is in this roster because of Baghban's four-name director field, and the search conducted for this batch resolved what that field most likely represents: he was an assistant director on the film, working under Ravi Chopra, and is otherwise known as a small-part actor in Baghban and Baabul and on television, reported in 2007 to be turning to direction. That finding substantiates the hypothesis recorded in batch 6 for Harish Razdan (PERSON-260), whose row could only note that nothing about him could be found — the likeliest reading is now that all three additional names in that infobox are assistants promoted into a credit they did not hold. The third, Yatin Dang, is PERSON-306. He should not be confused with the child actor billed as 'Master Vishal Desai' in the 1975 cast of Chupke Chupke, an unrelated name collision in this same filmography. Graded Low.

His identification required unpicking a wrong-article trap — a bare Wikipedia fetch of his name returns 'Vivek R. Shah', a well-formed article about an American businessman with no occurrences of 'film' and none of 'Bachchan', which is emphatically not this person. Bachchan's scenes in the film belong to the frame narrative Ram Gopal Varma directed, so the two men are credited on one film without having worked on any of the same material. Graded Low.

name: Vivek Sharma
career_background: Born on 27 August 1969 in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, an Indian filmmaker and script-writer. His article states that he became recognised when Amitabh Bachchan agreed to work on his directorial debut, and that he turned independent filmmaker in 2008 with that film.
debut: Bhoothnath (2008).
major_works: Bhoothnath (2008)
recurring_themes: Not determinable beyond one film — a children's ghost comedy in which the haunting turns out to be benign.
creative_style: No source characterises his direction beyond the debut.
major_awards: None located.
historical_importance: Slight; the film is remembered as a children's vehicle for Bachchan and spawned a sequel made by a different director.
relationship_with_actor: One film, and Bachchan is the reason it exists. Bhoothnath (2008) casts him as Kailash Nath, the ghost of a lonely old man haunting his own house, who is befriended rather than feared by a small boy; Juhi Chawla and Shah Rukh Khan also appear. His article states plainly that Sharma became recognised for his work when Bachchan agreed to be in his directorial debut — an unusually candid acknowledgement that the star made the career. Nitesh Tiwari (PERSON-275) directed the 2014 sequel, Bhoothnath Returns, again with Bachchan in the title role.
most_important_collaboration: Bhoothnath (2008), his only film with Bachchan.
biography: Vivek Sharma directed Bhoothnath in 2008, his debut, in which Amitabh Bachchan plays the ghost of an old man who haunts his house until a child befriends him — a children's film with Juhi Chawla and an appearance by Shah Rukh Khan, and the first of two Bhoothnath films, the sequel going to Nitesh Tiwari six years later. His article is short, ungrammatical and reads as promotional, calling the film 'one the biggest block buster', a characterisation the film's commercial record does not support and which is repeated here only as the article's own claim. Its more useful sentence is the frank one: that Sharma became recognised as a filmmaker because Bachchan agreed to appear in his first film. That is the whole substance of the relationship, and a clear instance of a late-career Bachchan credit functioning as a launch for a first-time director. Graded Medium.

biography: Yatin Dang is, with Harish Razdan, the least substantiated person in this roster of 306. He exists in the record in exactly one place — the director field of Baghban's Wikipedia infobox, which lists four names where every other source lists one — and phase 1 copied that field into the Films sheet, which is the sole reason this row exists. A search covering his name with the film and its director credit returned nothing at all: no article, no second credit, no birth date, no confirmation he worked on the picture. The batch-7 search for his co-listed Vishal Desai (PERSON-303) did establish that Desai was an assistant director on Baghban, which makes the likeliest explanation for all three extra names an editor promoting assistants into the infobox. The conflict is recorded rather than resolved, and the row is graded Unknown.
